sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: The Russian Revolution was a period of political and social change in Russia, starting in 1917.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: This period saw Russia abolish its monarchy and adopt a socialist form of government following two successive revolutions and a civil war.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: It can be seen as the precursor for other revolutions that occurred in the aftermath of World War I, such as the German Revolution of 1918–1919.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: The Russian Revolution was a key event of the 20th century.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: The Russian Revolution was inaugurated with the February Revolution in 1917, in the midst of World War I.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: With the German Empire inflicting defeats on the front, and increasing logistical problems causing shortages of bread and grain, the Russian Army was losing morale, with large scale mutiny looming.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: Officials were convinced that if Tsar Nicholas II abdicated, the unrest would subside.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: Nicholas stepped down on 15 March [O.S.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: 2 March], ushering in a provisional government led by the Duma (parliament).

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: During the unrest, Soviet councils were formed by locals in Petrograd (now Saint Petersburg) that initially did not oppose the new government; however, the Soviets insisted on their influence in the government and control over militias.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: By March, Russia had two rival governments.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: The Provisional Government held state power in military and international affairs, whereas the network of Soviets held domestic power.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: Critically, the Soviets held the allegiance of the working class, and urban middle class.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: There were mutinies, protests and strikes.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: Socialist and other leftist political organizations competed for influence within the Provisional Government and Soviets.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: Factions included the Mensheviks, Socialist Revolutionaries, Anarchists, and the Bolsheviks, a far-left party led by Vladimir Lenin.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: The Bolsheviks won popularity with their program promising peace, land, and bread: an end to the war, land for the peasantry, and ending famine.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: After assuming power, the Provisional Government continued fighting the war in spite of public opposition.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: Taking advantage, the Bolsheviks and other factions gained popular support to advance the revolution.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: Responding to discontent in Petrograd, the Provisional Government repressed protestors leading to the July Days.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: The Bolsheviks merged workers' militias loyal to them into the Red Guards.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: The volatile situation reached its climax with the October Revolution, a Bolshevik armed insurrection in Petrograd beginning 7 November [O.S.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: 25 October] that overthrew the Provisional Government.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: The Bolsheviks established their own government and proclaimed the establishment of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (RSFSR).

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: Under pressure from German military offensives, the Bolsheviks relocated the capital to Moscow.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: The RSFSR began reorganizing the empire into the world's first socialist state, to practice soviet democracy on a national and international scale.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: Their promise to end Russia's participation in World War I was fulfilled when Bolshevik leaders signed the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with Germany in March 1918.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: The Bolsheviks established the Cheka, a secret police and revolutionary security service working to uncover, punish, and eliminate those considered to be "enemies of the people" in campaigns called the Red Terror.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: Although the Bolsheviks held large support in urban areas, they had foreign and domestic enemies that refused to recognize their government.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: Russia erupted into a bloody civil war, which pitted the Reds (Bolsheviks), against their enemies, which included nationalist movements, anti-Bolshevik socialist parties, anarchists, monarchists and liberals; the latter two parties strongly supported the Russian White movement which was led mainly by right-leaning officers and seen as fighting for the restoration of the imperial order.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: The Bolshevik commissar Leon Trotsky began organizing workers' militias loyal to the Bolsheviks into the Red Army.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: While key events occurred in Moscow and Petrograd, every city in the empire was convulsed, including the provinces of national minorities, and in the rural areas peasants took over and redistributed land.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: As the war progressed, the RSFSR established Soviet power in Armenia, Azerbaijan, Byelorussia, Georgia, and Ukraine.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: Wartime cohesion and intervention from foreign powers prompted the RSFSR to begin unifying these nations under one flag and created the Soviet Union.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: Historians consider the end of the revolutionary period to be in 1922, when the civil war concluded with the defeat of the White Army and separatist factions, leading to mass emigration from Russia.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution
sentences.text: The victorious Bolshevik Party reconstituted itself into the All-Union Communist Party (Bolsheviks) and remained in power for six decades.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: The Russian Revolution of 1905 was a major factor contributing to the cause of the Revolutions of 1917.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: The events of Bloody Sunday triggered nationwide protests and soldier mutinies.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: A council of workers called the St. Petersburg Soviet was created in this chaos.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: While the 1905 Revolution was ultimately crushed, and the leaders of the St. Petersburg Soviet were arrested, this laid the groundwork for the later Petrograd Soviet and other revolutionary movements during the leadup to 1917.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: The 1905 Revolution also led to the creation of a Duma (parliament) that would later form the Provisional Government following February 1917.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Russia's poor performance in 1914–1915 prompted growing complaints directed at Tsar Nicholas II and the Romanov family.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: A short wave of patriotic nationalism ended in the face of defeats and poor conditions on the Eastern Front of World War I.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: The Tsar made the situation worse by taking personal control of the Imperial Russian Army in 1915, a challenge far beyond his skills.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: He was now held personally responsible for Russia's continuing defeats and losses.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: In addition, Tsarina Alexandra, left to rule while the Tsar commanded at the front, was German born, leading to suspicion of collusion, only to be exacerbated by rumors relating to her relationship with the controversial mystic Grigori Rasputin.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Rasputin's influence led to disastrous ministerial appointments and corruption, resulting in a worsening of conditions within Russia.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: After the entry of the Ottoman Empire on the side of the Central Powers in October 1914, Russia was deprived of a major trade route to the Mediterranean Sea, which worsened the economic crisis and the munitions shortages.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Meanwhile, Germany was able to produce great amounts of munitions whilst constantly fighting on two major battlefronts.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: The conditions during the war resulted in a devastating loss of morale within the Russian army and the general population of Russia itself.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: This was particularly apparent in the cities, owing to a lack of food in response to the disruption of agriculture.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Food scarcity had become a considerable problem in Russia, but the cause of this did not lie in any failure of the harvests, which had not been significantly altered during wartime.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: The indirect reason was that the government, in order to finance the war, printed millions of roubles, and by 1917, inflation had made prices increase up to four times what they had been in 1914.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Farmers were consequently faced with a higher cost of living, but with little increase in income.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: As a result, they tended to hoard their grain and to revert to subsistence farming.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Thus the cities were constantly short of food.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: At the same time, rising prices led to demands for higher wages in the factories, and in January and February 1916, revolutionary propaganda, in part aided by German funds, led to widespread strikes.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: This resulted in growing criticism of the government, including an increased participation of workers in revolutionary parties.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Liberal parties too had an increased platform to voice their complaints, as the initial fervor of the war resulted in the Tsarist government creating a variety of political organizations.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: In July 1915, a Central War Industries Committee was established under the chairmanship of prominent Octobrist, Alexander Guchkov (1862–1936), which included ten workers' representatives.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: The Petrograd Mensheviks agreed to join despite the objections of their leaders abroad.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: All this activity gave renewed encouragement to political ambitions, and in September 1915, a combination of Octobrists and Kadets in the Duma demanded the forming of a responsible government, which the Tsar rejected.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: All these factors had given rise to a sharp loss of confidence in the regime, even within the ruling class, growing throughout the war.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Early in 1916, Guchkov discussed with senior army officers and members of the Central War Industries Committee about a possible coup to force the abdication of the Tsar.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: In December, a small group of nobles assassinated Rasputin, and in January 1917 the Tsar's cousin, Grand Duke Nicholas, was asked indirectly by Prince Lvov whether he would be prepared to take over the throne from his nephew, Tsar Nicholas II.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: None of these incidents were in themselves the immediate cause of the February Revolution, but they do help to explain why the monarchy survived only a few days after it had broken out.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Meanwhile, Socialist Revolutionary leaders in exile, many of them living in Switzerland, had been the glum spectators of the collapse of international socialist solidarity.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: French and German Social Democrats had voted in favour of their respective governments' war efforts.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Georgi Plekhanov in Paris had adopted a violently anti-German stand, while Alexander Parvus supported the German war effort as the best means of ensuring a revolution in Russia.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: The Mensheviks largely maintained that Russia had the right to defend herself against Germany, although Julius Martov (a prominent Menshevik), now on the left of his group, demanded an end to the war and a settlement on the basis of national self-determination, with no annexations or indemnities.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: It was these views of Martov that predominated in a manifesto drawn up by Leon Trotsky (at the time a Menshevik) at a conference in Zimmerwald, attended by 35 Socialist leaders in September 1915.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Inevitably, Vladimir Lenin supported by Zinoviev and Radek, strongly contested them.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Their attitudes became known as the Zimmerwald Left.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Lenin rejected both the defence of Russia and the cry for peace.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background
sentences.text: Since the autumn of 1914, he had insisted that "from the standpoint of the working class and of the labouring masses the lesser evil would be the defeat of the Tsarist Monarchy"; the war must be turned into a civil war of the proletarian soldiers against their own governments, and if a proletarian victory should emerge from this in Russia, then their duty would be to wage a revolutionary war for the liberation of the masses throughout Europe.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: An elementary theory of property, believed by many peasants, was that land should belong to those who work on it.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: At the same time, peasant life and culture was changing constantly.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: Change was facilitated by the physical movement of growing numbers of peasant villagers who migrated to and from industrial and urban environments, but also by the introduction of city culture into the village through material goods, the press, and word of mouth.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: Workers also had good reasons for discontent: overcrowded housing with often deplorable sanitary conditions, long hours at work (on the eve of the war, a 10-hour workday six days a week was the average and many were working 11–12 hours a day by 1916), constant risk of injury and death from poor safety and sanitary conditions, harsh discipline (not only rules and fines, but foremen's fists), and inadequate wages (made worse after 1914 by steep wartime increases in the cost of living).

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: At the same time, urban industrial life had its benefits, though these could be just as dangerous (in terms of social and political stability) as the hardships.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: There were many encouragements to expect more from life.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: Acquiring new skills gave many workers a sense of self-respect and confidence, heightening expectations and desires.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: Living in cities, workers encountered material goods they had never seen in villages.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: Most importantly, workers living in cities were exposed to new ideas about the social and political order.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: The social causes of the Russian Revolution can be derived from centuries of oppression of the lower classes by the Tsarist regime and Nicholas's failures in World War I.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: While rural agrarian peasants had been emancipated from serfdom in 1861, they still resented paying redemption payments to the state, and demanded communal tender of the land they worked.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: The problem was further compounded by the failure of Sergei Witte's land reforms of the early 20th century.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: Increasing peasant disturbances and sometimes actual revolts occurred, with the goal of securing ownership of the land they worked.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: Russia consisted mainly of poor farming peasants and substantial inequality of land ownership, with 1.5% of the population owning 25% of the land.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: The rapid industrialization of Russia also resulted in urban overcrowding and poor conditions for urban industrial workers (as mentioned above).

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: Between 1890 and 1910, the population of the capital, Saint Petersburg, nearly doubled from 1,033,600 to 1,905,600, with Moscow experiencing similar growth.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: This created a new 'proletariat' which, due to being crowded together in the cities, was much more likely to protest and go on strike than the peasantry had been in previous times.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: One 1904 survey found that an average of 16 people shared each apartment in Saint Petersburg, with six people per room.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: There was also no running water, and piles of human waste were a threat to the health of the workers.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: The poor conditions only aggravated the situation, with the number of strikes and incidents of public disorder rapidly increasing in the years shortly before World War I.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: Because of late industrialization, Russia's workers were highly concentrated.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: By 1914, 40% of Russian workers were employed in factories of 1,000+ workers (32% in 1901).

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: 42% worked in 100–1,000 worker enterprises, 18% in 1–100 worker businesses (in the US, 1914, the figures were 18%, 47% and 35% respectively).

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: World War I added to the chaos.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: Conscription across Russia resulted in unwilling citizens being sent off to war.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: The vast demand for factory production of war supplies and workers resulted in many more labor riots and strikes.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: Conscription stripped skilled workers from the cities, who had to be replaced with unskilled peasants.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: When famine began to hit due to the poor railway system, workers abandoned the cities in droves seeking food.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: Finally, the soldiers themselves, who suffered from a lack of equipment and protection from the elements, began to turn against the Tsar.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Economic and social changes
sentences.text: This was mainly because, as the war progressed, many of the officers who were loyal to the Tsar were killed, being replaced by discontented conscripts from the major cities who had little loyalty to the Tsar.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Many sections of the country had reason to be dissatisfied with the existing autocracy.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Nicholas II was a deeply conservative ruler and maintained a strict authoritarian system.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Individuals and society in general were expected to show self-restraint, devotion to community, deference to the social hierarchy and a sense of duty to the country.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Religious faith helped bind all of these tenets together as a source of comfort and reassurance in the face of difficult conditions and as a means of political authority exercised through the clergy.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Perhaps more than any other modern monarch, Nicholas II attached his fate and the future of his dynasty to the notion of the ruler as a saintly and infallible father to his people.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: This vision of the Romanov monarchy left him unaware of the state of his country.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: With a firm belief that his power to rule was granted by Divine Right, Nicholas assumed that the Russian people were devoted to him with unquestioning loyalty.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: This ironclad belief rendered Nicholas unwilling to allow the progressive reforms that might have alleviated the suffering of the Russian people.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Even after the 1905 Revolution spurred the Tsar to decree limited civil rights and democratic representation, he worked to limit even these liberties in order to preserve the ultimate authority of the crown.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Despite constant oppression, the desire of the people for democratic participation in government decisions was strong.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Since the Age of Enlightenment, Russian intellectuals had promoted Enlightenment ideals such as the dignity of the individual and the rectitude of democratic representation.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: These ideals were championed most vociferously by Russia's liberals, although populists, Marxists, and anarchists also claimed to support democratic reforms.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: A growing opposition movement had begun to challenge the Romanov monarchy openly well before the turmoil of World War I.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Dissatisfaction with Russian autocracy culminated in the huge national upheaval that followed the Bloody Sunday massacre of January 1905, in which hundreds of unarmed protesters were shot by the Tsar's troops.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Workers responded to the massacre with a crippling general strike, forcing Nicholas to put forth the October Manifesto, which established a democratically elected parliament (the State Duma).

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Although the Tsar accepted the 1906 Fundamental State Laws one year later, he subsequently dismissed the first two Dumas when they proved uncooperative.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Unfulfilled hopes of democracy fueled revolutionary ideas and violent outbursts targeted at the monarchy.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: One of the Tsar's principal rationales for risking war in 1914 was his desire to restore the prestige that Russia had lost amid the debacles of the Russo-Japanese War (1904–1905).

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Nicholas also sought to foster a greater sense of national unity with a war against a common and old enemy.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: The Russian Empire was an agglomeration of diverse ethnicities that had demonstrated significant signs of disunity in the years before the First World War.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Nicholas believed in part that the shared peril and tribulation of a foreign war would mitigate the social unrest over the persistent issues of poverty, inequality, and inhumane working conditions.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > Political issues
sentences.text: Instead of restoring Russia's political and military standing, World War I led to the slaughter of Russian troops and military defeats that undermined both the monarchy and Russian society to the point of collapse.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: The outbreak of war in August 1914 initially served to quiet the prevalent social and political protests, focusing hostilities against a common external enemy, but this patriotic unity did not last long.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: As the war dragged on inconclusively, war-weariness gradually took its toll.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Although many ordinary Russians joined anti-German demonstrations in the first few weeks of the war, hostility toward the Kaiser and the desire to defend their land and their lives did not necessarily translate into enthusiasm for the Tsar or the government.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Russia's first major battle of the war was a disaster; in the 1914 Battle of Tannenberg, over 30,000 Russian troops were killed or wounded and 90,000 captured, while Germany suffered just 12,000 casualties.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: However, Austro-Hungarian forces allied to Germany were driven back deep into the Galicia region by the end of the year.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: In the autumn of 1915, Nicholas had taken direct command of the army, personally overseeing Russia's main theatre of war and leaving his ambitious but incapable wife Alexandra in charge of the government.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Reports of corruption and incompetence in the Imperial government began to emerge, and the growing influence of Grigori Rasputin in the Imperial family was widely resented.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: In 1915, things took a critical turn for the worse when Germany shifted its focus of attack to the Eastern Front.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: The superior German Army – better led, better trained, and better supplied – was quite effective against the ill-equipped Russian forces, driving the Russians out of Galicia, as well as Russian Poland during the Gorlice–Tarnów Offensive campaign.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: By the end of October 1916, Russia had lost between 1,600,000 and 1,800,000 soldiers, with an additional 2,000,000 prisoners of war and 1,000,000 missing, all making up a total of nearly 5,000,000 men.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: These staggering losses played a definite role in the mutinies and revolts that began to occur.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: In 1916, reports of fraternizing with the enemy began to circulate.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Soldiers went hungry, lacked shoes, munitions, and even weapons.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Rampant discontent lowered morale, which was further undermined by a series of military defeats.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Casualty rates were the most vivid sign of this disaster.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: By the end of 1914, only five months into the war, around 390,000 Russian men had lost their lives and nearly 1,000,000 were injured.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Far sooner than expected, inadequately trained recruits were called for active duty, a process repeated throughout the war as staggering losses continued to mount.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: The officer class also saw remarkable changes, especially within the lower echelons, which were quickly filled with soldiers rising up through the ranks.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: These men, usually of peasant or working-class backgrounds, were to play a large role in the politicization of the troops in 1917.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: The army quickly ran short of rifles and ammunition (as well as uniforms and food), and by mid-1915, men were being sent to the front bearing no arms.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: It was hoped that they could equip themselves with arms recovered from fallen soldiers, of both sides, on the battlefields.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: The soldiers did not feel as if they were valuable, rather they felt as if they were expendable.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: By the spring of 1915, the army was in steady retreat, which was not always orderly; desertion, plundering, and chaotic flight were not uncommon.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: By 1916, however, the situation had improved in many respects.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Russian troops stopped retreating, and there were even some modest successes in the offensives that were staged that year, albeit at great loss of life.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Also, the problem of shortages was largely solved by a major effort to increase domestic production.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Nevertheless, by the end of 1916, morale among soldiers was even worse than it had been during the great retreat of 1915.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: The fortunes of war may have improved, but the fact of war remained which continually took Russian lives.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: The crisis in morale (as was argued by Allan Wildman, a leading historian of the Russian army in war and revolution) "was rooted fundamentally in the feeling of utter despair that the slaughter would ever end and that anything resembling victory could be achieved."

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: The war did not only devastate soldiers.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: By the end of 1915, there were manifold signs that the economy was breaking down under the heightened strain of wartime demand.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: The main problems were food shortages and rising prices.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Inflation dragged incomes down at an alarmingly rapid rate, and shortages made it difficult for an individual to sustain oneself.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: These shortages were a problem especially in the capital, St. Petersburg, where distance from supplies and poor transportation networks made matters particularly worse.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Shops closed early or entirely for lack of bread, sugar, meat, and other provisions, and lines lengthened massively for what remained.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Conditions became increasingly difficult to afford food and physically obtain it.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Strikes increased steadily from the middle of 1915, and so did crime, but, for the most part, people suffered and endured, scouring the city for food.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Working-class women in St. Petersburg reportedly spent about forty hours a week in food lines, begging, turning to prostitution or crime, tearing down wooden fences to keep stoves heated for warmth, and continued to resent the rich.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Government officials responsible for public order worried about how long people's patience would last.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: A report by the St. Petersburg branch of the security police, the Okhrana, in October 1916, warned bluntly of "the possibility in the near future of riots by the lower classes of the empire enraged by the burdens of daily existence."

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I
sentences.text: Tsar Nicholas was blamed for all of these crises, and what little support he had left began to crumble.

sentences.text: As discontent grew, the State Duma issued a warning to Nicholas in November 1916, stating that, inevitably, a terrible disaster would grip the country unless a constitutional form of government was put in place.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Background > World War I

sentences.text: The next day, a series of meetings and rallies were held for International Women's Day, which gradually turned into economic and political gatherings.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: Demonstrations were organised to demand bread, and these were supported by the industrial working force who considered them a reason for continuing the strikes.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: Students, white-collar workers, and teachers joined the workers in the streets and at public meetings.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: To quell the riots, the Tsar looked to the army.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: At least 180,000 troops were available in the capital, but most were either untrained or injured.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: Historian Ian Beckett suggests around 12,000 could be regarded as reliable, but even these proved reluctant to move in on the crowd, since it included so many women.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: It was for this reason that on 11 March [O.S.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: 26 February], when the Tsar ordered the army to suppress the rioting by force, troops began to revolt.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: Although few actively joined the rioting, many officers were either shot or went into hiding; the ability of the garrison to hold back the protests was all but nullified, symbols of the Tsarist regime were rapidly torn down around the city, and governmental authority in the capital collapsed – not helped by the fact that Nicholas had prorogued the Duma that morning, leaving it with no legal authority to act.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: The response of the Duma, urged on by the liberal bloc, was to establish a Temporary Committee to restore law and order; meanwhile, the socialist parties established the Petrograd Soviet to represent workers and soldiers.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: The remaining loyal units switched allegiance the next day.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: The Tsar directed the royal train back towards Petrograd, which was stopped on 14 March [O.S.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: 1 March], by a group of revolutionaries at Malaya Vishera.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: When the Tsar finally arrived at Pskov, the Army Chief Nikolai Ruzsky, and the Duma deputies Alexander Guchkov and Vasily Shulgin suggested in unison that he abdicate the throne.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: He did so on 15 March [O.S.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: 2 March], on behalf of himself, and then, having taken advice on behalf of his son, the Tsarevich.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: But the Grand Duke realised that he would have little support as ruler, so he declined the crown on 16 March [O.S.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: 3 March], stating that he would take it only if that was the consensus of democratic action.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: Six days later, Nicholas, no longer Tsar and addressed with contempt by the sentries as "Nicholas Romanov", was reunited with his family at the Alexander Palace at Tsarskoye Selo.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: He was placed under house arrest with his family by the Provisional Government.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: The immediate effect of the February Revolution was a widespread atmosphere of elation and excitement in Petrograd.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: On 16 March [O.S.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: 3 March], a provisional government was announced.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: The center-left was well represented, and the government was initially chaired by a liberal aristocrat, Prince Georgy Yevgenievich Lvov, a member of the Constitutional Democratic Party (KD).

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: The socialists had formed their rival body, the Petrograd Soviet (or workers' council) four days earlier.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > February Revolution
sentences.text: The Petrograd Soviet and the Provisional Government competed for power over Russia.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The effective power of the Provisional Government was challenged by the authority of an institution that claimed to represent the will of workers and soldiers and could, in fact, mobilize and control these groups during the early months of the revolution – the Petrograd Soviet Council of Workers' Deputies.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The model for the Soviets were workers' councils that had been established in scores of Russian cities during the 1905 Revolution.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: In February 1917, striking workers elected deputies to represent them and socialist activists began organizing a citywide council to unite these deputies with representatives of the socialist parties.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: On 27 February, socialist Duma deputies, mainly Mensheviks and Socialist Revolutionaries, took the lead in organizing a citywide council.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The Petrograd Soviet met in the Tauride Palace, room 13, permitted by the Provisional Government.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The leaders of the Petrograd Soviet believed that they represented particular classes of the population, not the whole nation.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: They also believed Russia was not ready for socialism.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: They viewed their role as limited to pressuring hesitant "bourgeoisie" to rule and to introduce extensive democratic reforms in Russia (the replacement of the monarchy by a republic, guaranteed civil rights, a democratic police and army, abolition of religious and ethnic discrimination, preparation of elections to a constituent assembly, and so on).

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: They met in the same building as the emerging Provisional Government not to compete with the Duma Committee for state power, but to best exert pressure on the new government, to act, in other words, as a popular democratic lobby.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The relationship between these two major powers was complex from the beginning and would shape the politics of 1917.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The representatives of the Provisional Government agreed to "take into account the opinions of the Soviet of Workers' Deputies", though they were also determined to prevent interference which would create an unacceptable situation of dual power.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: In fact, this was precisely what was being created, though this "dual power" (dvoyevlastiye) was the result less of the actions or attitudes of the leaders of these two institutions than of actions outside their control, especially the ongoing social movement taking place on the streets of Russia's cities, factories, shops, barracks, villages, and in the trenches.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: A series of political crises took place in the relationship between the Provisional Government and the Soviets (which developed into a nationwide movement with a national leadership).

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The All-Russian Central Executive Committee of Soviets (VTsIK) undermined the authority of the Provisional Government but also of the moderate socialist leaders of the Soviets.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Although the Soviet leadership initially refused to participate in the "bourgeois" Provisional Government, Alexander Kerensky, a young, popular lawyer and a member of the Socialist Revolutionary Party (SRP), agreed to join the new cabinet, and became an increasingly central figure in the government, eventually taking leadership of the Provisional Government.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: As minister of war and later Prime Minister, Kerensky promoted freedom of speech, released thousands of political prisoners, continued the war effort, even organizing another offensive (which, however, was no more successful than its predecessors).

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Nevertheless, Kerensky still faced several great challenges, highlighted by the soldiers, urban workers, and peasants, who claimed that they had gained nothing by the revolution:

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The political group that proved most troublesome for Kerensky, and would eventually overthrow him, was the Bolshevik Party, led by Vladimir Lenin.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Lenin had been living in exile in neutral Switzerland and, due to democratization of politics after the February Revolution, which legalized formerly banned political parties, he perceived the opportunity for his Marxist revolution.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Although return to Russia had become a possibility, the war made it logistically difficult.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Eventually, German officials arranged for Lenin to pass through their territory, hoping that his activities would weaken Russia or even – if the Bolsheviks came to power – lead to Russia's withdrawal from the war.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Lenin and his associates, however, had to agree to travel to Russia in a sealed train: Germany would not take the chance that he would foment revolution in Germany.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: After passing through the front, he arrived in Petrograd in April 1917.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: On the way to Russia, Lenin prepared the April Theses, which outlined central Bolshevik policies.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: These included that the Soviets take power (as seen in the slogan "all power to the Soviets") and denouncing the liberals and social revolutionaries in the Provisional Government, forbidding co-operation with it.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Many Bolsheviks, however, had supported the Provisional Government, including Lev Kamenev.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: With Lenin's arrival, the popularity of the Bolsheviks increased steadily.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Over the course of the spring, public dissatisfaction with the Provisional Government and the war, in particular among workers, soldiers and peasants, pushed these groups to radical parties.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Despite growing support for the Bolsheviks, buoyed by maxims that called most famously for "all power to the Soviets", the party held very little real power in the moderate-dominated Petrograd Soviet.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: In fact, historians such as Sheila Fitzpatrick have asserted that Lenin's exhortations for the Soviet Council to take power were intended to arouse indignation both with the Provisional Government, whose policies were viewed as conservative, and the Soviets themselves, which were viewed as subservients to the conservative government.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: By some other historians' accounts, Lenin and his followers were unprepared for how their groundswell of support, especially among influential worker and soldier groups, would translate into real power in the summer of 1917.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: On 18 June, the Provisional Government launched an attack against Germany that failed miserably.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Soon after, the government ordered soldiers to go to the front, reneging on a promise.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The soldiers refused to follow the new orders.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The arrival of radical Kronstadt sailors – who had tried and executed many officers, including one admiral – further fueled the growing revolutionary atmosphere.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Sailors and soldiers, along with Petrograd workers, took to the streets in violent protest, calling for "all power to the Soviets".

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The revolt, however, was disowned by Lenin and the Bolshevik leaders and dissipated within a few days.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: In the aftermath, Lenin fled to Finland under threat of arrest while Trotsky, among other prominent Bolsheviks, was arrested.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The July Days confirmed the popularity of the anti-war, radical Bolsheviks, but their unpreparedness at the moment of revolt was an embarrassing gaffe that lost them support among their main constituent groups: soldiers and workers.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The Bolshevik failure in the July Days proved temporary.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The Bolsheviks had undergone a spectacular growth in membership.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Whereas, in February 1917, the Bolsheviks were limited to only 24,000 members, by September 1917 there were 200,000 members of the Bolshevik faction.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Previously, the Bolsheviks had been in the minority in the two leading cities of Russia – St. Petersburg and Moscow behind the Mensheviks and the Socialist Revolutionaries, by September the Bolsheviks were in the majority in both cities.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Furthermore, the Bolshevik-controlled Moscow Regional Bureau of the Party also controlled the Party organizations of the 13 provinces around Moscow.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: These 13 provinces held 37% of Russia's population and 20% of the membership of the Bolshevik faction.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: In August, poor and misleading communication led General Lavr Kornilov, the recently appointed Supreme Commander of Russian military forces, to believe that the Petrograd government had already been captured by radicals, or was in serious danger thereof.[dubious – discuss] In response, he ordered troops to Petrograd to pacify the city.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: To secure his position, Kerensky had to ask for Bolshevik assistance.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: He also sought help from the Petrograd Soviet, which called upon armed Red Guards to "defend the revolution".

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The Kornilov Affair failed largely due to the efforts of the Bolsheviks, whose influence over railroad and telegraph workers proved vital in stopping the movement of troops.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: With his coup failing, Kornilov surrendered and was relieved of his position.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The Bolsheviks' role in stopping the attempted coup further strengthened their position.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: In early September, the Petrograd Soviet freed all jailed Bolsheviks and Trotsky became chairman of the Petrograd Soviet.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Growing numbers of socialists and lower-class Russians viewed the government less as a force in support of their needs and interests.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The Bolsheviks benefited as the only major organized opposition party that had refused to compromise with the Provisional Government, and they benefited from growing frustration and even disgust with other parties, such as the Mensheviks and Socialist Revolutionaries, who stubbornly refused to break with the idea of national unity across all classes.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: In Finland, Lenin had worked on his book State and Revolution and continued to lead his party, writing newspaper articles and policy decrees.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: By October, he returned to Petrograd (present-day St. Petersburg), aware that the increasingly radical city presented him no legal danger and a second opportunity for revolution.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Recognising the strength of the Bolsheviks, Lenin began pressing for the immediate overthrow of the Kerensky government by the Bolsheviks.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: Lenin was of the opinion that taking power should occur in both St. Petersburg and Moscow simultaneously, parenthetically stating that it made no difference which city rose up first.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The Bolshevik Central Committee drafted a resolution, calling for the dissolution of the Provisional Government in favor of the Petrograd Soviet.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Dual power: Dvoyevlastiye
sentences.text: The resolution was passed 10–2 (Lev Kamenev and Grigory Zinoviev prominently dissenting) promoting the October Revolution.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > October Revolution
sentences.text: The October Revolution, which unfolded on 7 November [O.S.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > October Revolution

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > October Revolution
sentences.text: Lenin did not have any direct role in the revolution and he was hiding for his personal safety.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > October Revolution
sentences.text: However, in late October, Lenin secretly and at great personal risk entered Petrograd and attended a private gathering of the Bolshevik Central Committee on the evening of 23 October.

sentences.text: The Revolutionary Military Committee established by the Bolshevik party was organizing the insurrection and Leon Trotsky was the chairman.

sentences.text: 50,000 workers had passed a resolution in favour of Bolshevik demand for transfer of power to the soviets.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > October Revolution
sentences.text: However, Lenin played a crucial role in the debate in the leadership of the Bolshevik party for a revolutionary insurrection as the party in the autumn of 1917 received a majority in the soviets.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > October Revolution
sentences.text: An ally in the left fraction of the Revolutionary-Socialist Party, with huge support among the peasants who opposed Russia's participation in the war, supported the slogan 'All power to the Soviets'.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > October Revolution
sentences.text: The initial stage of the October Revolution which involved the assault on Petrograd occurred largely without any human casualties.[page needed]

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > October Revolution
sentences.text: Liberal and monarchist forces, loosely organized into the White Army, immediately went to war against the Bolsheviks' Red Army, in a series of battles that would become known as the Russian Civil War.

This non-elected provisional government faced the revolutionary situation and the growing mood against the war by avoiding elections to the state Duma.

sentences.text: Critics on the Right have long argued that the financial and logistical assistance of German intelligence via their key agent, Alexander Parvus was a key component as well, though historians are divided, since there is little evidence supporting that claim.

sentences.text: The elections to the Russian Constituent Assembly took place 25 November 1917.

sentences.text: The Bolsheviks gained 25% of the vote.

sentences.text: When it became clear that the Bolsheviks had little support outside of the industrialized areas of Saint Petersburg and Moscow, they simply barred non-Bolsheviks from membership in the Soviets.

sentences.text: The Bolsheviks dissolved the Constituent Assembly in January 1918.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Russian Civil War
sentences.text: The October Revolution led by the Bolsheviks was not recognized by a variety of social and political groups, including army officers and cossacks, the "bourgeoisie" and the landowners, and political groups ranging from the far Right to the moderate socialists, the Socialist Revolutionaries and the Mensheviks, who opposed the drastic restructuring championed by the Bolsheviks following the collapse of the Provisional Government.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Russian Civil War
sentences.text: The Russian Civil War, which broke out in the months following the revolution, resulted in the deaths and suffering of millions of people regardless of their political orientation.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Russian Civil War
sentences.text: The war was fought mainly between the Red Army ("Reds"), consisting of the Bolsheviks and the supporters of the Soviets, and the White movement ("Whites"), and their loosely allied "White Armies" led mainly by the right-leaning and conservative officers of the Russian Empire and the Cossacks and supported by the classes which lost their power and privileges with the Bolshevik revolution; the Civil War also included armed conflicts with nationalist movements for independence, armed struggle and terrorism by anti-Bolshevik socialists and anarchists, and uprisings of the peasants who organized themselves into the "Green armies".

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Russian Civil War
sentences.text: Although the views within the Russian Whites ranged from monarchism to socialism, the Whites generally preferred the Russian Empire to the revolution, and they were commonly seen as restorers of the old order as they fought the movements of the non-Russian nationalities in favour of "indivisible Russia" and opposed the land reform and defended the property rights of the upper classes; the socialists who opposed both factions saw the rule of the Whites (a military dictatorship headed by Alexander Kolchak and by the commanders of the White forces) as a right-wing dictatorship.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Russian Civil War
sentences.text: The Russian Whites had backing from other countries such as the United Kingdom, France, the United States, and Japan, while the Reds possessed internal support, proving to be much more effective.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Russian Civil War
sentences.text: Though the Allied nations, using external interference, provided substantial military aid to the Whites, they were ultimately defeated.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Russian Civil War
sentences.text: The Bolsheviks firstly assumed power in Petrograd, expanding their rule outwards.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Russian Civil War
sentences.text: They eventually reached the Easterly Siberian Russian coast in Vladivostok, four years after the war began, an occupation that is believed to have ended all significant military campaigns in the nation.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Russian Civil War
sentences.text: Less than one year later, the last area controlled by the White Army, the Ayano-Maysky District, directly to the north of the Krai containing Vladivostok, was given up when General Anatoly Pepelyayev capitulated in 1923.

sentences.text: Several revolts were initiated against the Bolsheviks and their army near the end of the war, notably the Kronstadt Rebellion.

sentences.text: This armed uprising was fought against the antagonizing Bolshevik economic policies that farmers were subjected to, including seizures of grain crops by the Communists.

sentences.text: This all amounted to large-scale discontent.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Russian Civil War
sentences.text: When delegates representing the Kronstadt sailors arrived at Petrograd for negotiations, they raised 15 demands primarily pertaining to the Russian right to freedom.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Russian Civil War
sentences.text: The Government firmly denounced the rebellions and labelled the requests as a reminder of the Social Revolutionaries, a political party that was popular among Soviets before Lenin, but refused to cooperate with the Bolshevik Army.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Russian Civil War
sentences.text: The Government then responded with an armed suppression of these revolts and suffered ten thousand casualties before entering the city of Kronstadt.

sentences.text: This ended the rebellions fairly quickly, causing many of the rebels to flee seeking political exile.

sentences.text: During the Civil War, Nestor Makhno led a Ukrainian anarchist movement.

sentences.text: Makhno's Insurgent Army allied to the Bolsheviks thrice, with one of the powers ending the alliance each time.

sentences.heading: Russian Revolution > Russian Civil War
sentences.text: However, a Bolshevik force under Mikhail Frunze destroyed the Makhnovshchina, when the Makhnovists refused to merge into the Red Army.

sentences.text: In addition, the so-called "Green Army" (peasants defending their property against the opposing forces) played a secondary role in the war, mainly in Ukraine.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Antiwar demonstrations
sentences.text: On 1–4 May, about 100,000 workers and soldiers of Petrograd, and, after them, the workers and soldiers of other cities, led by the Bolsheviks, demonstrated under banners reading "Down with the war!" and "All power to the soviets!"

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Antiwar demonstrations
sentences.text: The mass demonstrations resulted in a crisis for the Provisional Government.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Antiwar demonstrations

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Antiwar demonstrations

sentences.text: The Central Committee of the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party provided leadership to the spontaneous movements.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > July days

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > July days

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > July days
sentences.text: A period of repression followed.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > July days

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > July days
sentences.text: On 7 July, the government ordered the arrest and trial of Vladimir Lenin, who was forced to go underground, as he had done under the Tsarist regime.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > July days

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > July days

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > July days

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > July days

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > July days

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Kornilov affair
sentences.text: In what became known as the Kornilov affair, General Lavr Kornilov, who had been Commander-in-Chief since 18 July, with Kerensky's agreement directed an army under Aleksandr Krymov to march toward Petrograd to restore order.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Kornilov affair
sentences.text: According to some accounts, Kerensky appeared to become frightened by the possibility that the army would stage a coup, and reversed the order.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Kornilov affair
sentences.text: By contrast, historian Richard Pipes has argued that the episode was engineered by Kerensky.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Kornilov affair

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Kornilov affair
sentences.text: With few troops to spare at the front, Kerensky turned to the Petrograd Soviet for help.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Kornilov affair
sentences.text: Bolsheviks, Mensheviks, and Socialist Revolutionaries confronted the army and convinced them to stand down.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Kornilov affair
sentences.text: The Bolsheviks' influence over railroad and telegraph workers also proved vital in stopping the movement of troops.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Kornilov affair
sentences.text: The political right felt betrayed, and the left was resurgent.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Kornilov affair
sentences.text: The first direct consequence of Kornilov's failed coup was the formal abolition of the monarchy and the proclamation of the Russian Republic on 1 September.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Kornilov affair
sentences.text: With Kornilov defeated, the Bolsheviks' popularity in the soviets grew significantly, both in the central and local areas.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Background > Kornilov affair
sentences.text: On 31 August, the Petrograd Soviet of Workers and Soldiers Deputies—and, on 5 September, the Moscow Soviet Workers Deputies—adopted the Bolshevik resolutions on the question of power.

sentences.text: The Bolsheviks were able to take over in Briansk, Samara, Saratov, Tsaritsyn, Minsk, Kiev, Tashkent, and other cities.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Planning
sentences.text: On 10 October 1917 (O.S.; 23 October, N.S.), the Bolsheviks' Central Committee voted 10–2 for a resolution saying that "an armed uprising is inevitable, and that the time for it is fully ripe."

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Planning
sentences.text: At the Committee meeting, Lenin discussed how the people of Russia had waited long enough for "an armed uprising," and it was the Bolsheviks' time to take power.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Planning
sentences.text: Lenin expressed his confidence in the success of the planned insurrection.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Planning
sentences.text: His confidence stemmed from months of Bolshevik buildup of power and successful elections to different committees and councils in major cities such as Petrograd and Moscow.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Planning
sentences.text: Membership of the Bolshevik party had risen from 24,000 members in February 1917 to 200,000 members by September 1917.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Planning
sentences.text: The Bolsheviks created a revolutionary military committee within the Petrograd soviet, led by the Soviet's president, Leon Trotsky.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Planning
sentences.text: The committee included armed workers, sailors, and soldiers, and assured the support or neutrality of the capital's garrison.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Planning
sentences.text: The committee methodically planned to occupy strategic locations through the city, almost without concealing their preparations: the Provisional Government's President Kerensky was himself aware of them; and some details, leaked by Lev Kamenev and Grigory Zinoviev, were published in newspapers.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: In the early morning of 24 October (O.S.; 6 November N.S.), a group of soldiers loyal to Kerensky's government marched on the printing house of the Bolshevik newspaper, Rabochiy put (Worker's Path), seizing and destroying printing equipment and thousands of newspapers.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: Shortly thereafter, the government announced the immediate closure of not only Rabochiy put but also the left-wing Soldat, as well as the far-right newspapers Zhivoe slovo and Novaia Rus.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: The editors and contributors of these newspapers were seen to be calling for insurrection and were to be prosecuted on criminal charges.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: In response, at 9 a.m. the Bolshevik Military Revolutionary Committee issued a statement denouncing the government's actions.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: At 10 a.m., Bolshevik-aligned soldiers successfully retook the Rabochiy put printing house.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: Kerensky responded at approximately 3 p.m. that afternoon by ordering the raising of all but one of Petrograd's bridges, a tactic used by the government several months earlier during the July Days.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: What followed was a series of sporadic clashes over control of the bridges, between Red Guard militias aligned with the Military-Revolutionary Committee and military units still loyal to the government.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: At approximately 5 p.m. the Military-Revolutionary Committee seized the Central Telegraph of Petrograd, giving the Bolsheviks control over communications through the city.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: On 25 October (O.S.; 7 November, N.S.)

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: 1917, the Bolsheviks led their forces in the uprising in Petrograd (now St. Petersburg, then capital of Russia) against the Provisional Government.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: The event coincided with the arrival of a pro-Bolshevik flotilla—consisting primarily of five destroyers and their crews, as well as marines—in Petrograd harbor.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: At Kronstadt, sailors announced their allegiance to the Bolshevik insurrection.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: In the early morning, from its heavily guarded and picketed headquarters in Smolny Palace, the Military-Revolutionary Committee designated the last of the locations to be assaulted or seized.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: The Red Guards systematically captured major government facilities, key communication installations, and vantage points with little opposition.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: The Petrograd Garrison and most of the city's military units joined the insurrection against the Provisional Government.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: The insurrection was timed and organized to hand state power to the Second All-Russian Congress of Soviets of Workers' and Soldiers' Deputies, which began on this day.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: After the majority of the petrograd Soviet passed into the hands of the Bolsheviks, [Trotsky] was elected its chairman and in that position organized and led the insurrection of October 25.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: Kerensky and the Provisional Government were virtually helpless to offer significant resistance.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: Railways and railway stations had been controlled by Soviet workers and soldiers for days, making rail travel to and from Petrograd impossible for Provisional Government officials.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: The Provisional Government was also unable to locate any serviceable vehicles.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: On the morning of the insurrection, Kerensky desperately searched for a means of reaching military forces he hoped would be friendly to the Provisional Government outside the city and ultimately borrowed a Renault car from the American embassy, which he drove from the Winter Palace, along with a Pierce Arrow.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: Kerensky was able to evade the pickets going up around the palace and to drive to meet approaching soldiers.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: As Kerensky left Petrograd, Lenin wrote a proclamation To the Citizens of Russia, stating that the Provisional Government had been overthrown by the Military-Revolutionary Committee.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: The proclamation was sent by telegraph throughout Russia, even as the pro-Soviet soldiers were seizing important control centers throughout the city.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Onset
sentences.text: One of Lenin's intentions was to present members of the Soviet congress, who would assemble that afternoon, with a fait accompli and thus forestall further debate on the wisdom or legitimacy of taking power.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Assault on the Winter Palace
sentences.text: A final assault against the Winter Palace—against 3,000 cadets, officers, cossacks, and female soldiers—was not vigorously resisted.

sentences.text: The Bolsheviks delayed the assault because they could not find functioning artillery.

sentences.text: At 6:15 p.m., a large group of artillery cadets abandoned the palace, taking their artillery with them.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Assault on the Winter Palace
sentences.text: At 8:00 p.m., 200 cossacks left the palace and returned to their barracks.

sentences.text: While the cabinet of the provisional government within the palace debated what action to take, the Bolsheviks issued an ultimatum to surrender.

sentences.text: Workers and soldiers occupied the last of the telegraph stations, cutting off the cabinet's communications with loyal military forces outside the city.

sentences.text: As the night progressed, crowds of insurgents surrounded the palace, and many infiltrated it.

sentences.text: At 9:45 p.m, the cruiser Aurora fired a blank shot from the harbor.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Assault on the Winter Palace
sentences.text: Some of the revolutionaries entered the palace at 10:25 p.m. and there was a mass entry 3 hours later.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Assault on the Winter Palace
sentences.text: By 2:10 a.m. on 26 October, Bolshevik forces had gained control.
