sentences.text: The cadets and the 140 volunteers of the Women's Battalion surrendered rather than resist the 40,000 strong attacking force.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Assault on the Winter Palace
sentences.text: After sporadic gunfire throughout the building, the cabinet of the Provisional Government surrendered, and were imprisoned in Peter and Paul Fortress.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Assault on the Winter Palace
sentences.text: The only member who was not arrested was Kerensky himself, who had already left the palace.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Assault on the Winter Palace
sentences.text: With the Petrograd Soviet now in control of government, garrison, and proletariat, the Second All Russian Congress of Soviets held its opening session on the day, while Trotsky dismissed the opposing Mensheviks and the Socialist Revolutionaries (SR) from Congress.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Dybenko's disputed role
sentences.text: Some sources contend that as the leader of Tsentrobalt, Pavlo Dybenko played a crucial role in the revolt and that the ten warships that arrived at the city with ten thousand Baltic Fleet mariners were the force that took the power in Petrograd and put down the Provisional Government.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Dybenko's disputed role
sentences.text: The same mariners then dispersed by force the elected parliament of Russia, and used machine-gun fire against demonstrators in Petrograd, killing about 100 demonstrators and wounding several hundred.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Dybenko's disputed role
sentences.text: Dybenko in his memoirs mentioned this event as "several shots in the air".

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Dybenko's disputed role
sentences.text: These are disputed by various sources, such as Louise Bryant, who claims that news outlets in the West at the time reported that the unfortunate loss of life occurred in Moscow, not Petrograd, and the number was much less than suggested above.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Dybenko's disputed role
sentences.text: As for the "several shots in the air", there is little evidence suggesting otherwise.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Later Soviet portrayal
sentences.text: While the seizure of the Winter Palace happened almost without resistance, Soviet historians and officials later tended to depict the event in dramatic and heroic terms.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Later Soviet portrayal
sentences.text: The historical reenactment titled The Storming of the Winter Palace was staged in 1920.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Later Soviet portrayal
sentences.text: This reenactment, watched by 100,000 spectators, provided the model for official films made later, which showed fierce fighting during the storming of the Winter Palace, although, in reality, the Bolshevik insurgents had faced little opposition.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Later Soviet portrayal
sentences.text: Later accounts of the heroic "storming of the Winter Palace" and "defense of the Winter Palace" were propaganda by Bolshevik publicists.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Later Soviet portrayal
sentences.text: Grandiose paintings depicting the "Women's Battalion" and photo stills taken from Sergei Eisenstein's staged film depicting the "politically correct" version of the October events in Petrograd came to be taken as truth.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Later Soviet portrayal
sentences.text: Historical falsification of political events such as the October Revolution and the Brest-Litovsk Treaty became a distinctive element of Stalin's regime.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Later Soviet portrayal
sentences.text: A notable example is the 1938 publication, History of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union (Bolsheviks), in which the history of the governing party was significantly altered and revised including the importance of the leading figures during the Bolshevik revolution.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Later Soviet portrayal
sentences.text: Retrospectively, Lenin's primary associates such as Zinoviev, Trotsky, Radek, and Bukharin were presented as "vacillating", "opportunists" and "foreign spies" whereas Stalin was depicted as the chief discipline during the revolution.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Later Soviet portrayal
sentences.text: However, in reality, Stalin was considered a relatively unknown figure with secondary importance at the time of the event.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Later Soviet portrayal
sentences.text: In his book, The Stalin School of Falsification, Leon Trotsky argued that the Stalinist faction routinely distorted historical events and the importance of Bolshevik figures especially during the October Revolution.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Revolution > Later Soviet portrayal
sentences.text: He cited a range of historical documents such as private letters, telegrams, party speeches, meeting minutes, and suppressed texts such as Lenin's Testament.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Outcome > New government established
sentences.text: Lenin initially turned down the leading position of Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars when the Bolsheviks formed a new government, after the October Revolution in 1917, and suggested Trotsky for the position.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Outcome > New government established
sentences.text: However, Trotsky refused the position and other Bolsheviks insisted that Lenin assume principal responsibility which resulted in Lenin eventually accepting the role of chairman.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Outcome > New government established
sentences.text: The Second Congress of Soviets consisted of 670 elected delegates: 300 were Bolsheviks and nearly 100 were Left Socialist-Revolutionaries, who also supported the overthrow of the Alexander Kerensky government.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Outcome > New government established
sentences.text: When the fall of the Winter Palace was announced, the Congress adopted a decree transferring power to the Soviets of Workers', Soldiers' and Peasants' Deputies, thus ratifying the Revolution.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Outcome > New government established
sentences.text: The transfer of power was not without disagreement.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Outcome > New government established
sentences.text: The center and right wings of the Socialist Revolutionaries, as well as the Mensheviks, believed that Lenin and the Bolsheviks had illegally seized power and they walked out before the resolution was passed.

sentences.heading: October Revolution > Outcome > New government established
